title: Why Do Screens and Lights Flicker on Camera?
description:
Film a lamp or a screen with your phone and dark stripes can roll through the picture, while to your eyes the light looks steady. Many lights pulse twice per swing of the 50 or 60 Hz mains, 100 or 120 times a second, and many phone screens, and some laptop screens, dim by switching on and off (PWM). Your eyes blend it; a phone camera reads its sensor one row at a time (rolling shutter), so the pulses become stripes. They roll when the light's rhythm and the frame rate are out of step, the same aliasing as wheels that spin backwards on camera, and fade when each row's exposure holds whole pulses.

Try it: in a pro camera mode, film a flickering light at 1/1000 s, then at 1/100 s (or 1/120 s). Do the stripes go away?
